arm: H2 continuation history (retest of the arm rejected at 150 ms)
verdict: SHELVED. Screened NEGATIVE at 1000 ms: -8.7 Elo, 95% CI [-25.2, +7.8].
hypothesis: Plain history is already consumed by move ordering, so a term that restates it adds nothing (this is exactly why history-modulated LMR failed the same day). Continuation history is keyed by the PARENT move, so it can disagree with plain history and carry independent information. Previously measured +2.6 Elo at 150 ms and rejected on the harness later shown to understate depth-dependent arms ~2.3x.

implementation.table: cont_history: Vec<i32> of 64 * HIST_SIZE = 1,310,720 entries (5.2 MB per searcher, ~42 MB across Lazy SMP helpers)
implementation.key: parent move's destination square x move_index. A full (parent_move, move) table would be HIST_SIZE^2 and is unaffordable.
implementation.update: Mirrors the plain-history update -- gravity-bounded bonus on Bound::Lower for quiets, malus over tried_quiets.
implementation.ordering: Added to the flat sum, clamped to +/- CONT_HIST_CAP (4000).
implementation.why_a_cap_not_a_divisor: Ordering is a flat sum and a second history-magnitude term would let a saturated quiet outrank a winning capture -- the defect H4 fixed. A divisor was tried first and rejected on measurement: continuation values are small (p99 414, p50 -1), so dividing discards resolution exactly where the values live while only a rare tail approaches the bound. HIST_MAX + CONT_HIST_CAP = 20384 < GOOD_CAPTURE_PRIORITY + 1000 = 21000, asserted by a test.

the_signal_was_real.note: Unlike history-modulated LMR, this arm was NOT a structural no-op. The table genuinely fills and carries information plain history does not.
the_signal_was_real.read: 6x more non-zero entries than plain history at depth 11, and densifying with depth. The information exists.

measurement.harness: compare_play, 400 games, 1000 ms/move, paired openings, seed 20260818, 11 workers

why_it_still_lost.diagnosis: DEPTH DID NOT MOVE (12.92 -> 12.89) while NPS fell 4.1%. If the ordering term were helping, depth would rise at equal NPS. Instead the arm paid 4% throughput for a 5.2 MB sparse table -- cache pressure on a structure whose useful entries are 0.3% of its slots -- and recovered nothing in tree quality. Having information available is not the same as that information changing which move gets searched first, and the clamped contribution (p99 = 414 against a capture floor of 21000) is too small to reorder much.

process_correction.what_happened: The matein3 pre-screen said do not spend games: the node change was -0.127%, far below the 5% bar. That bar was OVERRIDDEN deliberately, on the argument that the suite is blind to this arm (the table is only 0.19% dense at depth 7 versus 0.34% at depth 11, and the same rule would have vetoed the Lazy SMP fix that proved worth +129 Elo).
process_correction.outcome: The override was WRONG and the rule was RIGHT. The pre-screen predicted a null result from the node count and the 400-game screen confirmed it, at a cost of ~1 hour.
process_correction.the_refined_rule: The Lazy SMP precedent does not generalise the way it was used here. matein3 is blind to changes it CANNOT express -- thread count, NPS, time management -- because it is single-threaded and fixed-depth. It is NOT blind to move-ordering changes, which are exactly what it measures: ordering changes the tree, and the tree is the node count. A <5% node change from an ORDERING arm is real evidence of a null result. Reserve the override for arms whose effect the suite structurally cannot express.

what_would_be_needed: Cheaper access. Most of the 4.1% NPS cost is cache pressure on a 1.3M-entry table that is 0.3% dense. A smaller key -- dropping HIST_PROMO_KINDS from the continuation index, or bucketing the parent square -- would shrink it ~5x. That is a real avenue but it only recovers the cost, and the arm also produced no depth gain to recover.

A stronger contribution. The clamped term is worth at most 4000 against a 21000 capture floor and a 1000-point capture bonus, so it can only reorder quiets among themselves. Raising it requires leaving the FLAT-SUM ordering for a tiered scheme (captures by SEE, then quiets by combined history), which is an architectural change and should be evaluated as one -- not smuggled in as a scaling constant.
Do not simply retry with a different cap. The null is corroborated by flat depth, which is independent of the cap.
caveats: 400-game screen only; no confirmation run, since the screen's lower bound did not clear zero and the point estimate was negative.
The CI spans zero, so this is 'not good enough to promote', not 'proven harmful'.

Measured against a baseline that already carries log-log LMR promoted earlier the same day. Continuation history might interact differently with the flat reduction it replaced, though there is no specific reason to expect so.
